newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $65, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $65, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle bids early Tuesday were light at $65.00 per cwt and passed by owners asking mostly $67.00, feedlot sources said.
Fed cattle sales this week were not expected until Wednesday or Thursday, with prices seen steady with last week's brisk sales at $66.00, several sources said.

Prices likely will not move higher because owners added extra cattle to this week's showlist to take advantage of the slight profitability that $66.00 sales brought to feedlots, some sources said. At $66.00, owners were breaking even to making up to $20.00 per head, they said.
Talk of higher fed cattle prices also was stymied by perceptions that beef prices were poised to trend lower following last week's steep advances, cattle feeders said.
"The market has a heavy feel to it," one Panhandle-area feedlot manager said.
Beef cut-out values Monday were quoted down $0.38 to up $0.09 per cwt, with 138 fabricated loads sold, USDA reported.
Heavyweight choice beef was quoted at $108.91, up $0.04 from Friday, USDA statistics showed.
